page.overview:
Who is Headless Demon?

The し|Kubi neshi oni}} was one of the dolls controlled by Mother of the Spider Family, deployed as her strongest weapon and a last resort against her confrontation with the Demon Slayer Corps. However, unlike Mother's other "dolls" which consisted of unwilling Demon Slayer manipulated by her threads, the Headless Demon was essentially a non-sentient marionette.

This demon was noted for its extremely tall and muscular frame, towering far above humans and possessing nearly the same stature as Father of the Spider Family. Its most distinct feature was its missing head, which, as indicated by the unclean wound along its neck, was likely ripped off by Mother in an attempt to keep the demon alive. Its two forearms appeared as bladed, spider-like legs that extend further than normal, giving the demon tremendous reach. Its skin was a dull purple, and had visible bulging veins throughout its body. The demon's only attire consisted of a pair of torn and weathered beige pants, with the left pant leg being completely torn open, and a loosely tied ribbon that acted somewhat like a belt.

This demon was one of the many demons found on Mount Natagumo. He was used as a puppet by Mother of Rui's Spider Family, being her last line of defense in case any threat got too close to her location. How he was transformed and what happened to his head, or if he was even a sentient demon in the first place is unknown.

During the mission on Mount Natagumo, after Tanjiro Kamado and Inosuke Hashibira saw their Demon Slayer Corps comrades die, they continued advancing in search of the demon responsible. Mother, seeing that they were about to find her, decided to release the Headless Demon, who was hanging, tangled in spiderweb threads. The Headless Demon was sent to attack them immediately upon encountering Tanjiro and Inosuke, initially surprising them by the absence of a neck they could cut with their katanas. However, Tanjiro quickly devised a solution: deploy a monk's hood cut to slash it diagonally through its torso.
